author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Colgate-Palmolive is exploring the sale of several mass-market personal-care brands, including Softsoap, Irish Spring and Speed Stick, Reuters reported Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. The company is working with Goldman Sachs on the possible divestiture.

The brands under review could bring in more than $1 billion, according to the sources. Colgate's broader personal-care business includes deodorants, soaps, shower gels and skin-care products, but the company is considering selling only part of the unit. Colgate and Goldman Sachs declined to comment to Reuters.

The review comes as major consumer-products companies reshape portfolios in response to tariffs, pressure on household spending and higher energy and input costs. Selling smaller brands can free capital and management attention for products a company considers central to future growth. A review does not guarantee a transaction, and no buyer or timetable was disclosed. Investors will be watching whether a sale proceeds, what valuation the brands receive and how Colgate would use any proceeds. The report concerns a potential deal, not a completed sale.
dek: Sources say the personal-care brands under review could fetch more than $1 billion as consumer groups narrow their portfolios.
headline: Colgate explores sale of Softsoap, Irish Spring and Speed Stick
